assignments.belief: Sister Ilva came down this morning white as linen — the chapel bell rang out alone in the dead of night, a summons no living soul would answer, as if the hill itself had called and been refused.
assignments.reasoning: Ilva walked down to the inn after dawn and told her friend the innkeeper, who turned a spare fact into an omen.

assignments.belief: Sister Ilva informed me the chapel bell was rung once after dark and that the door went unanswered. I have noted it; there is no evidence of intrusion.
assignments.reasoning: Ilva reported the irregularity to the garrison captain the next day, stripping it of fear and leaving only the facts.

assignments.belief: Maren told me the chapel bell rang and rang in the night and Sister Ilva stood at the door till dawn and nobody in the whole village would go up there.
assignments.reasoning: Maren passed the story to her stable boy later in the day, by which point it had lost the single ring and gained a night-long vigil.

assignments.belief: The bell rang once, long after dark. I waited at the door after it faded, and not a soul came.
assignments.reasoning: She was present at the chapel and experienced the ringing and the empty doorway firsthand.

assignments.belief: The woods were still last night. I have heard no news from the village in weeks.
assignments.reasoning: Bell lives half a day away in the deep woods with no social ties, so neither the sound nor any account can reach him.

summary: The unanswered night bell stayed with Ilva until morning, when she carried it down the hill to Maren as a story and to Osric as a report; Tam received a swollen version from Maren, and Bell never heard a thing.
